pages.text: A flat wagon that lays track: stacks of it show along its deck.

Click it for its store (27 slots; hoppers reach it too). Load it with $(item)Train Track$() and something to fill dips: stone, cobblestone, dirt or gravel (or deepslate, andesite, tuff, sandstone, netherrack...).$(br2)Couple it at the $(l)front$() of a train, drive to the end of the line and keep going: it lays track ahead of itself, holding the train to a walk.

It carries the line straight on, diagonals too. $(l)Steer$() left or right ($(k:key.left) / $(k:key.right)) and it lays a smooth 45° bend that way, then goes straight on: one bend for each press. Its screen sets the bends $(l)tight$() (about 10 blocks across) or $(l)wide$() (about 20).$(br2)It $(l)follows the ground$() up and down, at no more than 1 in 8; or, set to, it keeps the line $(l)level$().

Hills in the way are dug through, three wide: an open $(l)cutting$() where they're low, a $(l)tunnel$() where they're tall (its roof made good where sand or gravel would fall in, and water beside the line walled off). It keeps what it digs.$(br2)Dips up to six deep are $(l)filled$(), three wide, with stone, dirt or gravel.
Over a gully, filled three wide, and round a bend.

Deeper gaps, and water, are $(l)bridged$(): a deck under the line and a pier every four blocks down to the bottom (up to 48 deep). Load it with stone bricks or other bricks for them, or it uses fill.$(br2)Off the end of $(l:track/street_track)street track$(/l) it lays street track, with that aboard.
A bridge on piers, over a pool.

With $(l:electric/overhead_lines)masts and overhead wire$(/l) aboard, it $(l)wires the line$() too: a mast on its left every sixteen blocks or so, wire strung from the last, and its cuttings and tunnels dug tall enough for the wire.$(br2)It stops when it's out of track or fill, at water where the track would go, at a gap too deep even for a pier, and at bedrock, chests or other track right in the way.
Into a tall hill in a tunnel, wiring the line.

Its screen says why it's stopped, and so does a message to the driver.$(br2)The switch in its screen turns it off: then it's an ordinary wagon. The buttons under it set the slopes (following the ground, or level) and the bends (tight or wide).
Its screen: the store, the switch, what it's doing, and how it lays.
